newsitem.title: USA: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-LSU BEATS CLEMSON IN PEACH BOWL.
newsitem.headline: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-LSU BEATS CLEMSON IN PEACH BOWL.

text.p: Kevin Faulk ran for a touchdown and Wade Richey kicked a field goal to lead Louisiana State to a 10-7 victory over Clemson in the Peach Bowl at the Georgia Dome Saturday.

Clemson had a chance to tie it with just over a minute remaining, but LSU defensive end Arnold Miller blocked Matt Padgett's 52-yard field-goal attempt and safety Mark Roman returned it to the Clemson 47-yard line. Louisiana State quarterback Herb Tyler took a knee to run out the clock.

Quarterback Nealon Green's five-yard run gave Clemson a 7-0 lead with four seconds to go in the first quarter. Defensive end Trevor Pryce's blindside sack caused Tyler to fumble and linebacker Harold Means recovered at the LSU 10-yard line to set up the score.
Faulk's three-yard touchdown run tied it 7-7 just over two minutes into the second quarter.
Richey's 22-yard field goal ended the scoring with 4:35 left in the first half.

LSU had a chance to extend its lead, but tight end David LaFleur dropped a pass in the back of the end zone on 3rd-and-11 from the Clemson 23 midway through the third quarter. Pryce blocked Richey's 40-yard field-goal attempt and Clemson took over at its own 42.
Raymond Priester ran for 151 yards on 25 carries and became Clemson's all-time leading rusher, passing Kenny Flowers.
